Subject: RapidPay triage notes (initial)

Team — notes from the triage call with RapidPay (Ben + ops):

- Symptom summary: 95/99p latency spike to ~2s+, error-rate ~4-5%, observed time window 14:30–16:00 PDT. Affected model: rwd-gpt-large-v2 (reserved pool RP-7234).
- Observed infra signals: dedicated pool queue depth increased from median 12 -> 85; batch sizes increased (auto-batching reacting to headroom); KV cache miss rate jumped ~18% -> 62% for this workload (likely due to tokenization/sentence-shuffle pattern in their traffic).
- Immediate impact: their committed throughput (tokens/sec) is underperforming vs contract (measured shortfall ~26%).

Immediate mitigations we applied (15:50–16:00):
- Enabled short-term routing to compatible reserved fallback variant (rwd-gpt-large-v2-quant) for best-effort sessions (re-routed ~12% of traffic).
- Temporarily lowered default max_tokens for interactive sessions to 128 (reduces tail latency for many calls).
- Purged stale KV entries in the shared cache that were hot-spiky for this tenant.

Status: partial relief — P95 down to ~800ms but tail still flakey. Customer wants exec visibility. 

Next steps (proposed):
1) Aditya: deep root-cause analysis (kernel logs + scheduling traces) + estimate time to restore baseline.
2) Ops: consider temporary capacity bump (burst from general pool to their dedicated pool) — requires approval from capacity ops / finance for >8 GPU-hr.
3) Rishi/Naomi: prep a short exec note and timeline for RapidPay's leadership.

Attachments: kernel-logs-0505.txt (partial), request-rate-timeseries.png

—Rishi

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 00:42:37 -07:00
Subject: Re: RapidPay triage notes (initial) — infra analysis

Brief RCA (initial):
- Root cause signal: scheduler behaved normally but one availability group in the RapidPay dedicated pool experienced a misbalanced kernel placement after a model rolling task yesterday (placement mismatch caused uneven load on 2 GPUs). That, combined with this workload's high per-request KV-cache churn, produced localized queueing.
- Evidence: per-GPU token processing rate dropped 42% on gpu-12 vs pool median; context-switch logs show frequent small preempts while garbage-collection-ish mem compaction ran. See attached kernel snippets.

Short-term remediation (can be done in <2 hours):
- Live evacuate offending containers from gpu-12 -> redistribute across healthy nodes (need ops window). Estimated impact: restore ~70% of lost throughput within 40–60 minutes.
- If customer needs full baseline immediately, we can temporarily attach 2x spare GPUs from the shared burst pool to their reservation (cost ~8 GPU-hr) — needs exec approval.

Risk notes: evacuation causes transient reboots of containers (1–2 min per container) but we've done this safely before. Attaching extra GPUs requires a quick financial nod and will add temporary cost to their invoice; we should surface that to the customer.

—Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
